Key Plan.costume: A building surveyor: tin hat, tape measure on the belt, a roll of blueprints strapped across his back, one survey stake to carry. No arms, so the stake is tucked in the strap.

Link Blue.costume: a very small landlord with a clipboard, who has never once fixed anything.

Stet.costume: A proofreader's green eyeshade and a pencil behind where his ear would be, if he had one.

Dwell.costume: A surveyor in a hi-vis vest with a stake and a tape measure that reads `1 room` whatever you measure.

Painted Door.costume: a building inspector with a clipboard and a hard hat a size too small. No arms, so the clipboard hangs from a string round his neck.

Address Bar.costume: A very small moving man: flat cap, overalls, carrying one cardboard box marked "street (do not rebuild)". No hands, so the box just comes along.

Tear Here.costume: a mail carrier with a satchel holding one letter, addressed in full, finally.

Open Bracket.costume: a tired shop cashier: a plain tabard in dull coupon-paper cream, a name badge with nothing on it, a little hand-bell hanging at the front. No arms.

Full Stop.costume: A small-town comedy club's doorman: bow tie, cheap velvet jacket, a stopwatch on a string round his neck.

What's Prompted That.costume: A call-centre headset and a lanyard on a short-sleeved shirt and tie, plus a roll-up storage-unit door worn as a sandwich board, pulled halfway down.

After You.costume: A shop doorman: long coat, brass buttons, peaked cap, standing a little to one side of wherever he is, a small brass counter-clicker on his chest showing 4.

Well Documented.costume: A hostess in a good apron, carrying a salt shaker with total confidence.

That's Slugs.costume: A slug in a tiny hi-vis vest, holding a very small orange flag.

Breath In.costume: a sound engineer in headphones far too big, one cable going nowhere.

Falloff.costume: a lampshade, worn tilted, with a moth that never lands.
